title: Optimistic and pessimistic locking
context: What is the difference between optimistic and pessimistic locking?

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): Java concurrency questions (2 of 3)
source.note: Question and topic from this JavaGuide article. The answer is an original English write-up; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: Pessimistic locking assumes conflict is likely and locks the data before reading or updating it, for example with `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`. Others must wait. Optimistic locking assumes conflicts are rare. It reads a version or timestamp, and the update succeeds only if the version is unchanged (`UPDATE ... WHERE version = ?`). If not, it fails and the caller retries. Optimistic locking avoids holding locks and suits read-heavy work. Pessimistic locking suits high contention where retries would be wasteful.

points.title: Lock before or check after
points.why: Pessimistic locks the row first. Optimistic checks a version when writing.

points.title: Retry on conflict
points.why: Optimistic locking must handle a failed update by reloading and retrying.

points.title: Choose by contention
points.why: High contention favours pessimistic locks. Low contention favours optimistic ones.
